text:
Marathon Petroleum stock ticked up 0.66% today as crude oil prices fell sharply over the week on geopolitical de-escalation. U.S. crude dropped nearly 8% for the week after Iran and the U.S. held talks at the U.N., with Iran offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear negotiations—signals that reduced the risk of supply disruptions that had been priced into oil. For a refiner like this, lower crude costs are a double win: they cut input expenses while refining margins remain supported by strong demand and high utilization (refineries running at 94%).

The broader backdrop is mixed for refiners this week. Crude remains volatile—U.S. oil at $96/barrel versus world oil at $115 reflects lingering supply concerns—but the easing of Iran tensions has shifted sentiment away from a tight supply "super-cycle" hedge. Saudi Arabia is already ramping exports despite attacks on its infrastructure, adding supply. The stock's 2-week decline of 0.61% reflects the market recalibrating from earlier fears of prolonged geopolitical oil tightness.
